Recall that a linear congruence $ax≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ has a unique solution modulo $n$ if and only if $\text{gcd}(a,n)=1.$

In the given congruence, we have $a=35$ and $n=51$, where

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(35,51)=1.
$$

So, our congruence does indeed have a unique solution.

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $35\,(\text{mod}\,51).$ To find the inverse of $35\,(\text{mod}\,51)$, use the extended Euclidean algorithm.  

First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}51 & = & 35\cdot 1 & + & 16 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 35 & = & 16\cdot 2 & + & 3 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 16 & = & 3\cdot 5 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the rightmost terms in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}16 & =51-35\cdot 1 \\ 3 & =35-16\cdot 2 \\ 1 & =16-3\cdot 5.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =16-3\cdot 5 \\  & =16-(35-16\cdot 2)\cdot 5 \\  & =16\cdot 11-35\cdot 5 \\  & =(51-35)\cdot 11-35\cdot 5 \\  & =51\cdot 11-35\cdot 16 \\  & =51\cdot 11+35\cdot (-16)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have 

$$
1=51\cdot 11+35\cdot (-16).
$$

We can write this result in modulo $51,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}51\cdot 11+35\cdot (-16) & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,51) \\ 35\cdot (-16) & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,51) \\ 35\cdot (51-16) & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,51) \\ 35\cdot 35 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,51)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $35\cdot 35≡1\,(\text{mod}\,51),$ which means that 
$35$  is its own multiplicative inverse ( (modulo $51$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our original congruence by $35,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}35x & ≡5 &  & (\text{mod}\,51) \\ 35\cdot 35x & ≡35\cdot 5 &  & (\text{mod}\,51) \\ (35\cdot 35)x & ≡175 &  & (\text{mod}\,51) \\ 1\cdot x & ≡3\cdot 51+22 &  & (\text{mod}\,51) \\ x & ≡22 &  & (\text{mod}\,51)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x≡22\,(\text{mod}\,51).$
